proposals.issue_title: Fragile Image Generation & Lack of API Fallback Wrapper
proposals.current_pain_description: Pipelines rely on hardcoded API calls. If Pollinations has low quality, Together AI is rate-limited, or Gemini returns 429, the entire pipeline crashes. There is no unified logic to fallback from free APIs to low-cost paid ones (like Runware) while tracking the monthly 20€ budget.
proposals.proposed_fix: Create a unified `image_generator_engine.py` helper. It implements sequential fallback logic: Together AI (free Flux-schnell) -> Cloudflare Workers AI -> Runware (paid PAYG, capped to 20€/month maximum via a local state file tracking spend) -> Pollinations (free fallback). If all fail, it raises a clean exception instead of silently writing corrupted files.
proposals.estimated_value_unlocked: Eliminates pipeline crashes, optimizes image quality per prompt, and guarantees Hugo never exceeds his 20€ budget.

proposals.issue_title: Git Repository Bloat from Binary Assets on GitHub Actions
proposals.current_pain_description: Running image generation inside GitHub Actions and committing binary assets (.png, .jpg, .zip) directly to the Git repository will quickly exceed GitHub's 1GB-2GB recommended repository size limit, leading to repository lockout or slow Git performance on Termux.
proposals.proposed_fix: Modify pipelines to never commit raw high-res assets to the git history. Instead, have GitHub Actions package assets into a ZIP file and upload them to a GitHub Release draft (using the GitHub CLI `gh release create` which is pre-installed in GHA). Only commit lightweight metadata JSON files to the main branch.
proposals.estimated_value_unlocked: Keeps the Git repo under 50MB indefinitely, ensures rapid sync times on Hugo's Android Termux, and exploits free unlimited storage on GitHub Releases.

proposals.current_pain_description: Generating products is fully automated, but listing them on Redbubble, KDP, and Cults3D manually on an Android phone is highly tedious. Hugo spends hours copying/pasting tags, titles, descriptions, and pricing.
proposals.proposed_fix: Build a `metadata_packer.py` step at the end of every production pipeline. This script outputs a standardized `listing_package.json` and a formatted text file optimized for mobile copy-pasting (or a standard CSV compatible with bulk uploaders like Bulk Upload extensions), containing pre-translated localized descriptions, keywords, and category selections.
proposals.estimated_value_unlocked: Reduces listing time per product from 15 minutes to under 2 minutes, allowing Hugo to maintain volume within his 10h/week limit.

proposals.issue_title: Silent Failures and Zero-Byte/Corrupted Asset Generation
proposals.current_pain_description: When image APIs fail or return rate-limit HTML errors instead of binary images, pipelines sometimes write these HTML errors or empty bytes directly to `.png` files. This goes unnoticed until manual inspection, wasting GHA runtime.
proposals.proposed_fix: Integrate an automated validation step in the pipelines using Python's `PIL` (Pillow) library. Check if the generated file is a valid image, has a file size > 10KB, and check the image dimensions. If invalid, retry the generation or switch provider immediately.
proposals.estimated_value_unlocked: Prevents broken/corrupt assets from reaching Hugo's queue, saving manual review time on his phone.

proposals.issue_title: Lack of Checkpointing / State Serialization for Long-Running Pipelines
proposals.current_pain_description: To generate a 100-page coloring book, the pipeline must run 100 API image generation calls. If GHA timeouts (6 hours) or API limits are hit at page 85, the workflow fails, and all progress is lost, wasting API budget/quota on restart.
proposals.proposed_fix: Implement a checkpoint state JSON (e.g., `progress_state.json`) inside the pipeline's output directory. Before making an API call for an image or page, check if the file already exists and is valid. If yes, skip it. This allows safe retries and incremental generation over multiple GHA runs.
proposals.estimated_value_unlocked: Saves API limits and costs, allows building high-volume books incrementally, and provides resilience against network dropouts.

proposals.current_pain_description: Each pipeline acts in complete isolation. An asset generated for an SVG pack or a tumbler wrap is never reused for a coloring book background or a KDP paperback cover, forcing the system to generate new assets from scratch every time.
proposals.proposed_fix: Implement an `asset_shared_pool` directory structure. High-quality vector SVGs generated by the SVG pipeline are indexed in a central catalog. The KDP cover or Coloring Book pipelines can scan this catalog first to reuse existing vectors, applying automated filters (like turning SVG paths to black/white for coloring pages).
proposals.estimated_value_unlocked: Multiplies productivity: 1 base vector design is automatically repackaged into 3 different end-products (SVG Pack, Coloring Page, KDP Notebook Cover).
